# =============================================================================
# tessera-grid: wide characters, grapheme clusters, zero-width handling
#                 (issue #4, wave 3, milestone 0.1.0)
# crates/tessera-grid/tests/fixtures/wide_grapheme_spec.txt
#
# Evidence file for the implementer and the critic. Every row cites its source.
# It is test DATA, not a test: crates/tessera-grid/tests/wide.rs (layer: grid,
# layer: width) and crates/tessera-term/tests/wide.rs (layer: term) are written
# from it, same pattern as print.rs::fixture_cases_hold.
#
# HOW THE EXPECTED VALUES WERE PRODUCED
#   A throw-away Rust reference model (not committed) of the RECOMMENDED
#   algorithm below, linked against the exact crates in Cargo.lock:
#     unicode-width        0.2.2   (UNICODE_VERSION 17.0.0)  default features (cjk on,
#                                                             only width() is used)
#     unicode-segmentation 1.13.3  (UNICODE_VERSION 17.0.0)  graphemes(true)
#   The model asserts these invariants after every row (see INVARIANTS): paired
#   WIDE/SPACER, no CLUSTER on a spacer, cursor in bounds, pending_wrap only on the
#   last column. Every `cells:` block below was then read through by hand against
#   the rule cited on its row. `width` rows (section A) are raw library output, not
#   model output.
#   The sources were READ, not run: xterm, kitty, Alacritty and WezTerm behaviour is
#   quoted from their source (fetched 2026-10-27, master/main). No emulator was
#   executed, so "xterm does X" below means "charproc.c / screen.c / util.c say X".
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (short tags used in `cite:` lines)
#   UAX11   https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr11/      EastAsianWidth: sec 4 (properties),
#                                                      sec 5 (F, W => 2 cells; Na, H, N => 1;
#                                                      A => 1 outside an East Asian context)
#   UAX29   https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr29/      sec 3.1.1 Grapheme Cluster Boundary
#                                                      Rules GB1..GB999 (GB4/5 controls, GB6-8
#                                                      Hangul, GB9 Extend|ZWJ, GB9a SpacingMark,
#                                                      GB9b Prepend, GB9c Indic conjunct,
#                                                      GB11 emoji ZWJ, GB12/13 RI pairs).
#                                                      Emoji_Modifier is GCB=Extend (Table 2).
#   UTS51   https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr51/      1.4.2 ED-6 Emoji_Presentation; 1.4.3
#                                                      ED-8a text / ED-9a emoji presentation
#                                                      sequences (VS15 / VS16); 1.4.4 ED-12 modifier
#                                                      base, ED-13 modifier sequence; 1.4.5 ED-14
#                                                      flag, ED-14a tag, ED-14c keycap, ED-16 ZWJ
#                                                      sequence; 2.4 (a modifier after a non-base is
#                                                      free-standing); 2.5 (ZWJ fallback); 4.1
#   UW      unicode-width 0.2.2 src/lib.rs "Rules for determining width", rule numbers
#                                                      1 (string ligatures: emoji ZWJ, modifier,
#                                                      presentation sequences, scripts) and 2.1-2.7
#                                                      (char sums; 2.4 zero width; 2.5 F/W = 2;
#                                                      2.7 everything else 1)
#                   ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/unicode-width-0.2.2/src/lib.rs
#   XT      https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots (master)
#                   charproc.c  doparsing() zero-width block (combining attaches to the
#                               last written cell, else the cursor cell), dotext() (width
#                               accounting, WrapLine, DECAWM off), WrapLine()
#                   screen.c    ScrnWriteText() (overwriting half a wide char blanks the other
#                               half), ClearCells() (erase widens to whole wide chars),
#                               ScrnInsertChar()/ScrnDeleteChar() (DamagedCells + ClearCells)
#                   util.c      addXtermCombining() under OPT_EMOJI_WIDTH (VS15 shrink /
#                               VS16 increase base), WriteText() (INSERT => InsertChar)
#                   ptyx.h      ResetWrap() (cursor motion clears char_was_written)
#   KT      https://github.com/kovidgoyal/kitty/blob/master/kitty/screen.c
#                   draw_text_loop(), draw_combining_char(), widen_cell_to_two()
#   WZ      https://github.com/wezterm/wezterm/blob/main/term/src/terminalstate/performer.rs
#                   flush_print() (grapheme segmentation, zero-width elision, wrap_next)
#   AL      https://github.com/alacritty/alacritty/blob/master/alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs
#                   input() (zerowidth, LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER, WIDE_CHAR_SPACER),
#                   write_at_cursor() (clears the other half)
#   VT510   https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/IRM.html  and  .../DECAWM.html
#   brief   the wave-3 brief for #4 ("brief dd N" = its Design decision N)
#   print_c0_spec  crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/print_c0_spec.txt (issue #5)
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROW SYNTAX
#   A row starts with `### <ID>_<name>` and ends at the next `###` (comment lines that
#   start with `# ---` between rows are section headers; skip every line starting with '#').
#   Keys: `layer:` `size: RxC` (rows x cols, as in print_c0_spec) `step:` (repeatable, in
#   order) `input:` (width rows) `cite:` `note:` `flags:` and the result keys below.
#
#   layer: width   input -> char_widths / str_width / grapheme_scalar_counts, the raw
#                  library answers. Assert them with UnicodeWidthChar::width (none => None),
#                  UnicodeWidthStr::width and UnicodeSegmentation::graphemes(s, true)
#                  (scalar count of each grapheme). These pin the library version: a
#                  failing width row after a dependency bump is the point of the row.
#   layer: grid    steps drive tessera_grid::Grid directly (DECAWM is implicitly on, there
#                  is no insert mode at this layer).
#   layer: term    steps drive tessera_term::Terminal (tests/wide.rs in tessera-term; the
#                  result is read back from terminal.grid()).
#
#   Payload escapes (put / feed / feed_bytewise):
#       \u{H..}  one scalar     \\  backslash     \r  CR     \n  LF (term layer only)
#   House rule of this file: a zero-width scalar (UnicodeWidthChar::width == Some(0)) is
#   ALWAYS written \u{..}; everything else is literal. A decoder must panic on any other
#   escape so typos cannot hide.
#
#   Grid steps (-> API)
#     put <payload>        Grid::put_str / put_char per scalar
#     goto R C             Grid::goto (0-based, clamps, clears pending_wrap)
#     cr / lf              Grid::carriage_return / Grid::line_feed (LF keeps the column)
#     ich N / dch N / ech N      insert_chars / delete_chars / erase_chars
#     el to_end|to_start|all     erase_in_line(EraseLine::ToEnd|ToStart|All)
#     ed below|above|all         erase_in_display(Below|Above|All)
#     pen_bg N|none        set the pen to Style { bg: Color::Indexed(N), ..DEFAULT } (none =
#                          back to the default pen); fg/flags stay default
#     reset                Grid::reset
#   Term steps (-> API)
#     feed <payload>       one Terminal::advance call with the payload's UTF-8 bytes
#     feed_bytewise <p>    one advance call PER BYTE (chunk independence)
#     set auto_wrap true|false / set insert_mode true|false    Terminal::set_*
#   The term layer also uses the grid-layer results format; `\r` and `\n` are the only
#   controls that occur.
#
#   RESULT BLOCK (state after the last step)
#     cells:               one `>` line per grid row (the `>` is not part of the line).
#                          Cells are separated by exactly one space. A cell is a token:
#                            .            blank: ' ', no flags, no table entry
#                            ~            SPACER (right half of a wide cell)
#                            X            plain cell, literal char (no flags)
#                            X/W          WIDE base (a SPACER follows in the next column)
#                            X+HHHH+HHHH/C   or  /WC   CLUSTER: base char X, then the further
#                                         scalars of Line::cluster(col) as 4+ digit hex.
#                                         Line::cluster(col) is Some(X + the scalars) exactly
#                                         at these columns and None everywhere else (incl.
#                                         spacers).
#                            U+00A0       a whitespace base is written as U+HHHH, and so is a
#                                         width-1 Prepend format character (U+0600..0604,
#                                         U+06DD, U+110BD, U+110CD)
#                          A trailing `@N` means the cell's bg is Color::Indexed(N); no `@`
#                          means bg Default. Only bg is rendered: fg/attrs are default in every
#                          row. Separately assert, in a styled unit test, that a WIDE cell and
#                          its SPACER have equal Style (brief dd2: the spacer carries the whole
#                          Style, not just the bg).
#     cursor: (r,c)        0-based Grid::cursor() ; the issue text quotes 1-based
#     pending_wrap: b      Grid::pending_wrap()
#     wrapped_rows(0-based): [..]    rows whose Line::wrapped is true (NOTE: 0-based here,
#                          1-based in print_c0_spec)
#     scrollback: len=N [first=("text", wrapped=b)]   Grid::scrollback_len(), scrollback_line(0)
#     text:                one `>` line per row = Line::text() with width-0 scalars and
#                          non-space whitespace written \u{..}. Line::text() emits cluster text,
#                          SKIPS spacers, and trims trailing blanks (a blank is a plain ' '
#                          cell; a spacer or a CLUSTER cell is never trailing-blank).
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RECOMMENDED SEMANTICS (what the model implements; D-numbers are explained below)
#
#   Cell model     Cell { ch, style, flags: WIDE | SPACER | CLUSTER } ; Line::graphemes maps
#                  column -> full cluster text (base included) iff CLUSTER. A CLUSTER entry
#                  always has >= 2 scalars (a lone scalar is a plain cell). WIDE at c <=> SPACER
#                  at c+1. The pair never straddles the end of a line. A base is never ' '
#                  (see the attach gate) so a CLUSTER cell is never blank. "blank" below means
#                  Cell::blank_with(pen): ' ', default fg, bg = pen.bg, no flags, no entry.
#                  Recommended: Cell::is_blank is true only for a plain blank (no flags).
#
#   put_char(ch)   w = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch); None => return (controls).
#     1. ATTACH   if plan_attach(ch) succeeds, apply it and return.            (D4 D7)
#     2. if w == 0: drop it, return.                                           (D5)
#     3. NEW CELL
#          w == 2: if cols < 2 drop it (a wide char never fits a 1-column grid; no loop).
#                  if pending_wrap: wrap.
#                  else if cursor.col == cols-1 (one column left): blank the last column
#                  (split rule first) and wrap.                                 (D1)
#                  then split-fix both columns, write WIDE at c and SPACER at c+1 (SPACER has
#                  the same Style as the base), advance 2; if that reaches the line end the
#                  cursor stays on the last column with pending_wrap armed.
#          w == 1: if pending_wrap: wrap. split-fix, write, advance 1 (existing behaviour).
#        wrap = mark the row `wrapped`, CR, line_feed (scrolling at the bottom of the region).
#        split-fix(c), run before cell c is overwritten: if cell c is WIDE blank c+1; if cell
#        c is a SPACER blank c-1. An overwritten cell loses its CLUSTER entry.
#
#   plan_attach(ch)   (pure; this is the Grid::would_attach query, D8)
#        b  = pending_wrap ? cursor.col : cursor.col-1   (no left cell => no attach)
#        if cell b is a SPACER: b -= 1                  (the base of the wide cell)
#        fail if cell b is ' '                           (D7: blanks never take a scalar)
#        old = Line::cluster(b) or the base char ;  fail if old has >= 32 scalars   (D6)
#        new = old + ch
#        fail if unicode_segmentation::graphemes(new, true).count() != 1   (UAX29)
#        raw = UnicodeWidthStr::width(new)
#        fail if raw > 2 and old does NOT contain U+200D         (D4: after a ZWJ any width is ok)
#        nw = clamp(raw, 1, 2) ;  ow = cell b is WIDE ? 2 : 1
#        fail if nw > ow and b+1 >= cols                      (D3: no room to grow)
#      apply: cluster text := new (CLUSTER set; column b is the key).
#        nw > ow (grow):  split-fix(b+1); b becomes WIDE; b+1 becomes SPACER (Style of b);
#                         cursor := b+2, or the last column with pending_wrap armed if b+2 == cols.
#        nw < ow (shrink): b loses WIDE; b+1 becomes a blank (pen bg); cursor := b+1,
#                         pending_wrap := false.
#        nw == ow: nothing moves (cursor and pending_wrap unchanged).
#
#   Edits (all clear pending_wrap, like the existing grid; "blank" = pen background)
#     left boundary L of a range (first erased/deleted cell): if cell L is a SPACER blank L-1.
#     right boundary R (last erased cell): if cell R is WIDE blank R+1.
#     ECH(n) [c,c+n): left(c) + right(c+n-1) then blank the range.
#     EL to_end [c,cols): left(c).   EL to_start [0,c]: right(c).   EL all / ED: whole lines.
#     DCH(n): left(c); shift left (cluster entries move with their cells); the cell that lands in
#             column c, if a SPACER, is blanked (its base was deleted); pad the tail with blanks.
#     ICH(n): left(c); shift right (entries move); the cell that lands in column c+n, if a
#             SPACER, is blanked; if the last column now holds a WIDE base, blank it (its
#             spacer fell off the line); the n inserted cells are blanks.
#
#   tessera-term State::print (layer: term), recommended order; this is everything the term
#   must add on top of the grid:
#        if ch.is_control(): drop                                  (existing)
#        if grid.would_attach(ch): grid.put_char(ch); return       (NO wrap, NO goto, NO insert)
#        w = width(ch); if w == 0: return ; if w == 2 && cols < 2: return
#        if !auto_wrap:
#            if pending_wrap: grid.goto(row, cols-1)               (existing)
#            if w == 2 && cursor.col == cols-1: return             (D2)
#        else if insert_mode && (pending_wrap || (w == 2 && cursor.col == cols-1)):
#            if !pending_wrap: grid.erase_chars(1)                 (D1: blank the stranded column)
#            wrap_line()                                           (existing)
#        if insert_mode: grid.insert_chars(w)
#        grid.put_char(ch)
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommended option first)
#   D1  Wide char with one column left, DECAWM on (C01-C06, C15, H04).
#       Recommend: blank the stranded last column with the PEN background, mark the row
#       wrapped, write on the next row (Alacritty LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER). The brief says
#       this is xterm: it is not, xterm leaves the stranded cell untouched (dotext() just
#       WrapLines). Blanking matters because the cell would otherwise be copied out as part of
#       the wrapped line (C04, C05). Needs no DECAWM knowledge in the grid. Alternative:
#       leave it untouched (xterm, kitty).
#   D2  Wide char with one column left (or pending), DECAWM OFF (C07-C11, C16).
#       Recommend: drop the character, change nothing, pending_wrap cleared (xterm + Alacritty
#       drop). Alternative: kitty moves the char left to cols-2 and overwrites. NOT the brief's
#       hypothesis "overwrite the last column with a blank": nothing in xterm does that.
#       The grid never sees this case: it is decided in State::print (it owns DECAWM).
#   D3  Cluster GROWTH (1 -> 2: RI pair, VS16, SpacingMark; D03, D07-D13, D34).
#       Recommend: (a) if column b+1 exists, the SPACER is written over whatever is in b+1 (a
#       left-half there orphans its spacer, D08); text to the right is NEVER shifted, not even in
#       insert mode (H08 documents the one-cell loss). (b) if the base is in the LAST column
#       there is no room: the scalar is NOT attached; a zero-width one is dropped (D13), a
#       width-1 one (the 2nd RI) is an ordinary char (D10, H14, H15). No relocation of the base,
#       so the grid needs no DECAWM knowledge and no scrolling inside attach.
#       Alternatives: kitty relocates the whole cluster to the next row; xterm (OPT_EMOJI_WIDTH)
#       blanks the BASE ("disallow wrapping via VS16") and, reading `cur_col < max_col`, also
#       refuses when the filler would land in the last column (looks like an off-by-one,
#       D09 expects the opposite); attach-without-growth (keeps the VS16 in copied text).
#       SHRINK (2 -> 1: VS15 on a wide emoji; D16, D17): base loses WIDE, old spacer becomes a
#       blank, cursor moves to b+1, pending cleared (kitty halve_multicell_width, xterm 'shrink').
#   D4  ATTACH GATE for a scalar with width > 0 or a width change. UAX29 alone is not enough:
#       a + U+1F3FD is ONE grapheme of width 3, hangul L+L one grapheme of width 4, and the
#       transient prefix woman+ZWJ+heart (before the VS16) is width 3 while the finished
#       sequence is 2. Recommend: attach iff (single UAX29 grapheme) AND (raw width <= 2 OR the
#       cluster already contains a ZWJ); cell width = clamp(raw, 1, 2). Consequences: a modifier
#       after a non-base, a 2nd modifier, a modifier after a wide non-base and L+L jamo are NOT
#       attached and become their own cells (D24, D26, D27, D32); every RGI ZWJ sequence stays 2
#       cells (D02, D20, D21). Alternatives: pure UAX29 (3 or 4 columns of content in 2 cells), or
#       xterm/Alacritty style "only width-0 scalars attach" (skin tones, flags, ZWJ joins become
#       separate cells).
#   D5  A zero-width scalar that does not attach is DROPPED: nothing to its left (column 0, also
#       after CR or a soft wrap: E05-E07), blank left cell (E12, E13), GCB=Control format
#       characters ZWSP / WJ / BOM / SHY (E16, E18), refused by the gate (E21, D13), lone jungseong
#       filler. Only the width-1 Prepend characters (U+0600..0604, U+06DD, U+110BD, U+110CD)
#       take a cell, and under GB9b they join whatever scalar follows, a space included, into a
#       2-column cluster (D36, library-derived; column sums still match the library). The
#       width-0 ones (U+0605, U+070F, U+0890..0891, U+08E2, U+0D4E, U+111C2..111C3, U+113D1,
#       U+1193F, U+11941, U+11A84..11A89, U+11D46, U+11F02) are dropped like any zero-width
#       scalar that does not attach.
#   D6  Cluster size cap: 32 scalars per cluster text (E21). Longest RGI sequence is 10 scalars;
#       xterm caps combining characters at 2 by default (max 5). Pick any cap, but pick one:
#       Zalgo text must not grow a line's table without bound.
#   D7  Attach TARGET. Recommend: the cell left of the cursor (the cell under the cursor when
#       pending_wrap is armed), resolved through a SPACER to its base, and only if it is not ' '.
#       No last-written memory, never the previous row. Costs: SPACE + mark loses the mark (E13;
#       NBSP + mark works, E14) and a mark after cursor motion over text attaches to the text
#       left of the cursor (E15). kitty and WezTerm drop marks after any cursor motion; xterm
#       attaches to the cell AT the cursor; Alacritty to the cursor cell/left cell and at column 0
#       even to cell (0,0). The brief's "previous row's last column when the row is wrapped"
#       (dd4) is NOT recommended (E07).
#   D8  API gap: State::print needs a pure query `Grid::would_attach(ch) -> bool` (or the
#       equivalent) because insert / wrap / goto must be skipped for attaching scalars. Three
#       traps in the existing print(): H05 (modifier is width 2 but attaches: insert_chars(2) opens
#       a gap), H07 (insert_mode && pending_wrap wraps for ANY char, including a mark), H12
#       (!auto_wrap && pending_wrap does goto(last col), which clears pending and redirects the
#       mark to column cols-2). The brief's public_api list has no such method.
#   D9  VS15/VS16 on a base that is not an emoji (D14): recommend attach, width unchanged
#       (UAX29 GB9, kitty). xterm DROPS the selector unless the base is an emoji (mk_is_emoji).
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ISSUE TEXT CORRECTIONS (verified against source)
#   1. brief dd6: "wrap first, leaving the last column blank with the pen background (xterm)".
#      xterm does not blank it (charproc.c dotext(): width_here 2 > width_available 1, no write,
#      WrapLine() sets LINEWRAPPED and indexes). Blanking is Alacritty's behaviour. Recommended
#      anyway (D1).
#   2. brief dd6 "DECAWM off -> xterm overwrites the last column with a blank and drops the
#      character... verify". Verified: xterm drops the wide char and writes nothing. But note
#      xterm's dotext() works on a whole buffer: with DECAWM off it copies the buffer's LAST
#      character into the last column (`buf[chars_chomped + offset - 1] = buf[len - 1]`), so
#      "abcd中X" delivered in one write gives "abcX" in xterm and "abcdX" per-character. The
#      fixture (C07-C11, C16) follows the per-character model; xterm is not an oracle beyond
#      "the wide char is not written".
#   3. brief Risks: "unicode-width 0.2 treats ... RI pairs as 2". Only for the STRING. A single
#      regional indicator is width 1 (EAW=N, no special rule), so every flag is a 1 -> 2 growth
#      case (A13, D03) and a lone RI is a narrow cell (D04). The same applies to ASCII + VS16
#      (keycaps, A25) and SpacingMarks (A29).
#   4. brief dd3/dd4 "a scalar that, appended to the cluster ..., forms a single grapheme per UAX
#      #29 attaches" is necessary but not sufficient: see D4 (width gate), D5 (what happens to a
#      zero-width scalar that does not attach), D3 (growth room), D8 (the term needs the query).
#   5. The brief lists xterm charproc.c as the wide-character reference. xterm handles combining
#      (width-0) characters and, with OPT_EMOJI_WIDTH, VS15/VS16, but never clusters ZWJ
#      sequences, skin tones or regional indicators: those scalars get cells of their own. Rows
#      D01-D03, D20-D22, D24-D27 are therefore kitty / WezTerm / UAX29 / unicode-width driven, not
#      xterm driven. WezTerm clusters whole print batches (Graphemes::new over the buffered
#      text), so it is not an incremental oracle either; kitty is (grapheme_segmentation_step).
#   6. UnicodeWidthStr::width counts each C0/C1 control as width 1 while UnicodeWidthChar::width is
#      None for it (A15). Only the char API may be used to decide "ignore this scalar".
#   7. Width is NOT the EastAsianWidth property alone: U+1160 and U+11A8.. are EAW=W/N but width
#      0 (Hangul V/T jamo), U+115F is 2, U+0600 (Prepend) is 1, U+00AD is 0 (UW 0.2.2 rules 2.1-
#      2.7). Always call the crate.
#   8. Unchecked: the brief's claim that the old render WIDE table mis-classifies 245 code
#      points. It concerns tessera-render, not this fixture.
#
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INVARIANTS for a proptest (the existing bounds.rs strategy plus put of arbitrary chars,
# ZWJ, VS15/16, marks, modifiers, RIs, ich/dch/ech/el/ed, scroll, goto)
#   I1  every WIDE cell at column c has c+1 < cols and a SPACER at c+1.
#   I2  every SPACER at c has c > 0 and a WIDE cell at c-1.
#   I3  graphemes keys == { c : cell c has CLUSTER }; each entry has 2..=32 scalars; a SPACER
#       never has CLUSTER; entry[0] == cell.ch.
#   I4  no scalar is lost or duplicated by attach: for a lone put_str of a single grapheme the
#       concatenated Line::text() equals the input (modulo dropped zero-width scalars).
#   I5  cursor.col < cols, cursor.row < rows; pending_wrap implies cursor.col == cols-1.
#   I6  Line::text() contains no U+0020 produced by a SPACER, and its display width
#       (sum of UnicodeWidthStr over clusters) never exceeds cols.
#   I7  feeding a payload in one advance() or one byte per advance() gives identical grid state.
# =============================================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- A. Widths (library facts the grid must reproduce)

### A01_cjk_ideograph_is_wide
layer: width
input: 中
cite: UAX11 sec 5 (EastAsianWidth W => 2 cells); UW 0.2.2 rules 2.5
char_widths: [2]
str_width: 2
grapheme_scalar_counts: [1]

### A02_fullwidth_latin_is_wide
layer: width
input: Ａ
cite: UAX11 sec 5 (EAW=F => 2 cells); UW 0.2.2 rules 2.5
char_widths: [2]
str_width: 2
grapheme_scalar_counts: [1]

### A03_halfwidth_katakana_is_narrow
layer: width
input: ｱ
cite: UAX11 sec 5 (EAW=H => 1 cell); UW 0.2.2 rules 2.7
char_widths: [1]
str_width: 1
grapheme_scalar_counts: [1]

### A04_hangul_syllable_is_wide
layer: width
input: 한
cite: UAX11 sec 5 (EAW=W); UW 0.2.2 rules 2.5
char_widths: [2]
str_width: 2
grapheme_scalar_counts: [1]

### A05_hangul_conjoining_jamo_L_V_T
layer: width
input: ᄒ\u{1161}\u{11AB}
cite: UAX11 (L jamo EAW=W); UW 0.2.2 rules 2.4 (Hangul_Syllable_Type V and T are width 0); UAX29 GB6/GB7/GB8 (one grapheme)
note: Leading jamo is 2 cells, vowel and trailing jamo add 0: the three scalars are one 2-cell grapheme.
char_widths: [2, 0, 0]
str_width: 2
grapheme_scalar_counts: [3]

### A06_supplementary_plane_cjk
layer: width
input: 𠀀

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- C. Wide character with one column left / DECAWM


### C01_wide_with_one_column_left_wraps_and_blanks_last_col
layer: grid
size: 3x5
step: put abcd中
cite: xterm charproc.c dotext() (width_here 2 > width_available 1 => WrapLine() before writing, LINEWRAPPED set); alacritty term/mod.rs input() (writes a LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER blank in the last column); kitty screen.c draw_text_loop (continue_to_next_line when columns < x + char_width)
note: Cursor is on the last column (not pending) with 1 column left. Recommended: blank the stranded last column with the pen background, mark row 0 wrapped, write at (1,0). xterm itself leaves the cell untouched (see ISSUE TEXT CORRECTIONS 1). D1.
cells:
>a b c d .
>中/W ~ . . .
>. . . . .
cursor: (1,2)
pending_wrap: false
wrapped_rows(0-based): [0]
scrollback: len=0
text:
>abcd
>中
>
